section: Science · Ch — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: A ramp used to roll a heavy drum up onto a truck, allowing the same work to be done with less force applied over a longer distance, is an example of which simple machine?
explanation: An inclined plane trades distance for force — pushing a load up a slope needs less force than lifting it straight up, though the same total work is done since the load travels a longer path.

section: Science · Ch — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: A screwdriver's handle turning a narrow shaft, or a doorknob turning a spindle, both work on the principle of which simple machine, where a larger circle rotates to move a smaller circle rigidly attached to it?
explanation: A wheel and axle consists of a large wheel rigidly fixed to a smaller axle; turning the wheel (handle/doorknob) with modest force produces a larger turning force at the axle — a common mechanical-advantage device.

section: Science · Ch — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: A wood screw, or a spiral staircase winding upward around a central pole, both function as which simple machine — essentially an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder?
explanation: A screw is an inclined plane wound helically around a cylindrical core; each turn advances the screw a fixed distance, converting rotational force into a strong linear/gripping force — used in screws, bolts, and spiral staircases.
